group_assessment.weighting: Two rodent absence-epilepsy models (WAG/Rij rat, DBA/2J mouse; 141 rats and 44 mice, both sexes), video-ECoG, glucometry, insulin and thalamic 2-deoxyglucose, slice patch-clamp, AMPK FRET reporter, systemic metformin. Primary for thalamic AMPK-GABAB biology, not for WWOX and not for any neonatal infusion or feeding regimen. The observations (more spike-wave seizures after an 18 h fast, after insulin, after thalamic 2-DG or A-769662; lethal seizures after 200 mg/kg metformin in WAG/Rij only) are firm as reported for those models; the AMPK-GABAB mechanism is the authors' proposed framework and is not measured in vivo (no in vivo p-AMPK, no GABAB antagonist rescue of the in vivo effect).

entries.proposition: The main text gives P = 0.0078 for the WAG/Rij spike-wave count after fasting and calls it nearly 2-fold.
entries.snippet: SWS count was nearly 2-fold higher during the fasted versus fed recording sessions for WAG/Rij rats (P = 0.0078, n = 13; Fig. 1F).

entries.proposition: Table S1 gives the WAG/Rij fasted-versus-fed spike-wave count as 21.9 versus 34.9 (ratio about 1.6) with P = 0.0044, n = 13; the value 0.0078 sits in the DBA row (n = 10). The main-text P value belongs to the mouse row.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Table S1 (supplement PDF page 1): DBA row SWS count 3.2 versus 9.4, N 10, p 0.0078; WAG row SWS count 21.9 versus 34.9, N 13, p 0.0044; WAG blood glucose 114.1 versus 75.4 mg/dL, beta-hydroxybutyrate 1.1 versus 3.3 mM.
entries.anchor: Supplement Table S1, WAG and DBA rows

experimental_context.system: WAG/Rij rat (Table S1 WAG row) versus DBA/2J mouse (Table S1 DBA row)
experimental_context.endpoint: spike-wave seizure count, fed versus 18 h fasted

entries.proposition: The fast was set to produce at least a 30% fall in blood glucose.
entries.snippet: On Day 3, animals fasted for 18 h, a duration required to achieve at least a 30% drop in blood glucose.

entries.proposition: Fasting raised seizure count and burden but not seizure duration.
entries.snippet: The increased seizure burden was largely driven by an elevated seizure count, not an increase in SWS duration (P = 0.17, n = 13; Fig. 1G).

entries.proposition: Figure 1I, J panels: fasting glucose about 75 against about 113 mg/dl fed, beta-hydroxybutyrate about 3.3 against about 1.2 mM; panel F count about 39 against 23 per 4 h.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 1F, I, J: SWS per 4 h about 23 fed and 39 fasted; glucose about 113 fed and 75 mg/dl fasted; beta-hydroxybutyrate about 1.2 fed and 3.3 mM fasted; panel K regression lines not significant.

experimental_context.endpoint: spike-wave count, blood glucose, serum beta-hydroxybutyrate

entries.proposition: In WAG/Rij rats, across pooled fed and fasted sessions, correlations of seizure count with glucose (p = 0.094) and beta-hydroxybutyrate (p = 0.49) were not significant (trends only); in DBA/2J mice the beta-hydroxybutyrate correlation was significant (p = 0.020, Table S1).
entries.snippet: While correlation coefficients were not statistically significant, SWS count and β-hydroxybutyrate trended towards a positive correlation, whereas SWS count and blood glucose trended towards an inverse correlation (Fig. 1K).

contradicts_locator.what_changed: scope restricted to rats; mouse result added from Table S1

entries.snippet: Insulin injection produced a large reduction in blood glucose (P = 0.0039, n = 9; Fig. 2G), whereas β-hydroxybutyrate remained unchanged relative to saline injection (P = 0.36, n = 9; Fig. 2H).

entries.proposition: The authors conclude hypoglycaemia is sufficient to increase spike-wave seizures, inferred from consistency across fasting and insulin and a significant inverse correlation in the mouse insulin data only.
entries.snippet: As the inverse relationship between SWS count and blood glucose was consistent across fasting and insulin experiments, we concluded that hypoglycaemia is sufficient to increase SWSs.
Comparing total SWS count during active delivery (i.e. pump turned on) showed that 2-DG infusion doubled SWS count, relative to saline (P = 0.010, n = 9; Fig. 2L).
